elements.honest: This is memorising names and numbers for a class or for fun. It does not teach chemistry. Keep the table open next to it when you study the real subject.

roots.honest: Roots help you make an educated guess about a new word, and guesses are sometimes wrong, because words drift from their roots. Use them to start, and check a dictionary. This is practice with word parts, not a way to learn a whole vocabulary quickly.

atlas.honest: Capitals are a classic cue-and-answer fact set and a good first use of pictures and rooms. Learning them says nothing about a country. The list reflects the usual situation and may change; check a current atlas.

music.honest: Music is learned by ear and hands. Pictures hold the fixed lists in the theory: the order of sharps, the lines of a clef, the intervals. They do not make you play or hear better.

chess.honest: Strong players learn openings through ideas and games, not by rote. Pictures help you hold the order of a line you chose to learn. They do not teach you why the moves are good and do not make you better at chess.
chess.notation: Algebraic notation: K king, Q queen, R rook, B bishop, N knight, no letter for a pawn, lower case letter and number for the square. 1.e4 means White moves a pawn to e4.

body.honest: This is the vocabulary students are asked to learn in an anatomy course. It is study terminology only. It is not health information and it does not help anyone judge a symptom. See a health professional for any health question.
body.edge: Some books call nerve XI the spinal accessory nerve, and some list carpal bones starting from a different side. Accept "Accessory" and "Spinal accessory".
